nodes.name: Electrodeposition of CoP on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: The CoP mesoporous nanorod arrays are fabricated via a potentiostat electrodeposition way in a three-electrode mode, in which Ni foam performs as the working electrode (see synthesis details in the Supporting Information). The highly conductive Ni foam permits the electron to continuously transfer through the whole framework, initializing the effective reduction of Co²⁺ and H₂PO₂⁻ to give a net reaction to yield CoP. The preliminarily formed CoP with good conductivity can facilitate the further nucleation, causing the generation of CoP nanorods with synchronously emerged mesopores inside.

nodes.source_text: Polarization curves from linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) tests... CoP-MNA is able to render current densities of 10, 100, and 800 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials (η) of 54, 121, and 235 mV... Tafel slope of 51 mV dec⁻¹... exchange current density... 0.857 mA cm⁻²... Accelerated degradation studies after continuous cyclic voltammogram (CV) scanning for 5000 cycles... 6.8 % cathodic current loss... chronoamperometric response... 6.5 % within 32 h... The Tafel slope, derived from the plot of log(R_CT^{-1}) versus η, is 58 mV dec⁻¹

LSV polarization curves (2 mV s⁻¹ in O₂ saturated 1 M KOH)... sharp onset potential at approximately 1.50 V... overpotential to deliver a 10 mA cm⁻² current density... only about 1.52 V... Tafel slope of 65 mV dec⁻¹... Faradaic efficiency of 97.3 %... chronopotentiometric response curve... nearly steady potential at about 1.54 V to give a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uneven surface for CoP nanorods with nanoparticles aggregation leaving interparticle mesopores of several nanometers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transition electron microscopy (TEM) image shows the uneven surface for the CoP nanorods (Figure 1g), and a closer look by high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) (Figure 1h) presents different domains resulted from the tight aggregation of nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern matches orthorhombic CoP phase structure (JCPDS No. 29-0497) with weak diffraction intensity indicating small CoP size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A series of diffraction peaks on the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of CoP-MNA match well with orthorhombic CoP phase structure (JCPDS No. 29-0497) (Figure 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 sorption isotherm is type IV with H2 hysteresis indicating ink-bottle-like mesopores; BJH pore size distribution shows maximum at 4 nm; BET specific surface area 148 m² g⁻¹, total pore volume 0.224 cm³ g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 sorption isotherm recorded on CoP-MNA is of typical type IV with a hysteresis loop of type H2... The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area is determined to be 148 m² g⁻¹, along with a total pore volume of 0.224 cm³ g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p₃/₂ peaks at 778.2 and 781.2 eV with satellites at 783.8, 785.6 eV; Co 2p₁/₂ at 796.9 eV with satellite at 802.7 eV indicating Co²⁺; P 2p doublet at 129.3/130.2 eV (CoP) and 133.6 eV (phosphate).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Peak deconvolution of the Co 2p₃/₂ core level region shows two main peaks at 778.2 and 781.2 eV and two satellites at 783.8 and 785.6 eV, respectively, while the Co 2p₁/₂ region shows one main peak at 796.9 eV... For the high-resolution P 2p spectrum... a weak doublet situated at 129.3 and 130.2 eV... and another contribution at 133.6 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER HRTEM shows nanoparticles of several nm with lattice fringes of cobalt oxo/hydroxo species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Highmagnification TEM image in Figure 6a demonstrates a number of nanoparticles with a size of several nanometers surrounding CoP after water oxidation, possessing clear lattice fringes indicative of registry order or crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Co 2p shows negative shift of main peak by 1.1 eV indicating transition to higher oxidation states; P 2p shows only phosphate at 133.1 eV, phosphide peaks disappear; O 1s at 531.1 eV (hydroxyls) and 529.6 eV (oxides/hydroxides).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution XPS spectra of Co 2p core level (Figure 6b), the post-OER CoP-MNA electrode engenders a negative shift of the main peak (about 1.1 eV)... Two intense bands in the O 1s core level at 531.1 and 529.6 eV... the change in the P state... a single peak located at 133.1 eV is ascribed to phosphate species, as well as the complete disappearance of the phosphide components around the binding energy of 130 eV.
